successors.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
successors.text: Bohemia, raised to a kingdom in 1198 (infobox)

ledger.x: c. 870: the Czech duchy of Bořivoj I arises inside the Moravian realm. 'It was formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm'; Bořivoj's reign 'is believed to have started about the year 870'. Moravian suzerainty from about 872 is in the Great Moravia dossier's ledger (vassal_start).
Winter 890: Svatopluk of Moravia takes over the Bohemian duchy.
June 895: the Bohemian dukes swear fealty to Arnulf and leave the Moravian realm.

c. 947: Boleslaus I's conquests take in Silesia. 'Assuming the Bohemian throne in 935, Duke Boleslaus conquered the adjacent lands of Moravia and Silesia.' The page gives no year for the conquest; 947 is Cliopatria's. Piast Poland borders it on the north and east.
955: after Lechfeld Boleslaus I receives Moravia.

c. 960: Boleslaus I's reach extends to Kraków. 'By occupying the city of Kraków, he controlled important trade routes from Prague to Kiev and Lviv.' The page gives no year; 960 is Cliopatria's. The Mieszko page calls Czech rule over Lesser Poland 'only nominal'. Cliopatria's 44,000 km2 addition also reaches west…
990: Mieszko I of Poland takes Silesia and Lesser Poland from Bohemia.
1003: Bolesław I the Brave of Poland takes Bohemia.
1004: the Poles are expelled from Bohemia with Henry II's help and Duke Jaromír receives the duchy in fief from the king.
1182: Moravia is made a margraviate of its own.

1197: the last year of the duchy; in 1198 'Duke Ottokar I ensured his elevation by the German king Philip of Swabia' and the duchy 'was raised to a hereditary Kingdom of Bohemia', which the kingdom-of-bohemia dossier (found 1198, counterpart this slug) draws.

wars.name: Boleslaus I's war with Otto I
wars.outcome: Boleslaus stopped paying tribute, 'in 936 moved into Thuringia'; in 950 Otto I besieged a castle held by Boleslaus's son and Boleslaus 'recognized Otto's suzerainty and promised to resume the payment of the tribute'.

wars.name: Battle of Lechfeld
wars.outcome: Bohemian troops fought as Otto I's allies; 'after the defeat of the Magyars [Boleslaus] received the lands of Moravia in recognition of his services'.

wars.name: Bohemian-Polish conflict over Silesia and Lesser Poland
wars.outcome: Mieszko I took Silesia (annexation 'possibly ... around 985', 'taken over by Poland' after the 990 war) and Lesser Poland (possibly before 990); Bohemia's rule over Lesser Poland had been 'only nominal'.

certainty.note: The Bohemian basin is bounded by mountains and the frontier is approximate throughout; the conquests east (Silesia, Kraków) are soft and, per the Mieszko page, partly nominal; no treaty line is on any page opened.
